text:
Refining PARAMS within the current topology is the best use of the 2 remaining LLM calls; I'm not editing the program.

**Why TC got worse.** The 10 MΩ divider pulls a roughly constant current (vx/RDIV, about 0.13 µA) out of the PTAT output branch. That makes the current through R2 and Q3 no longer purely PTAT, which lowers the effective PTAT gain and moves the zero-TC point. The simulated TC sensitivity supports this: +10% on `k_r2` cuts TC by 23%. Raising `k_r2` should rebalance PTAT against CTAT.

**Line regulation.** It is most sensitive to `gmid_n`, `gmid_p`, `Lp` and `k_r2`, so I'm widening those bounds too.

**Known issues not addressed.** Start-up device MS is off and MSN is in triode, but simulated start-up passes. The 27 °C simulation also logged gmin-stepping convergence failures.
